evidence.claim: The President has broad executive authority and the armed forces operate under the President's supreme authority, which defines Bolsonaro's 2022 decision space.
evidence.title: Constituição da República Federativa do Brasil
evidence.excerpt: The President has broad executive authority and the armed forces operate under the President's supreme authority, which defines Bolsonaro's 2022 decision space.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Authoritative constitutional text; directly states presidential powers and military command relation.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Bolsonaro held this office throughout 2022; the source is institutional rather than personal.
contrary_evidence: Legal authority does not show how Bolsonaro used it in nuclear or existential-risk matters.

evidence.claim: Presidents elected in 2022 took office on January 1, 2023, so Bolsonaro remained in office through all of 2022.
evidence.title: Emenda Constitucional nº 111
evidence.excerpt: Presidents elected in 2022 took office on January 1, 2023, so Bolsonaro remained in office through all of 2022.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary constitutional amendment with an explicit transition rule.
evidence.period_fit: Directly defines the end-of-2022 transition boundary.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Institutional constraint on Bolsonaro's final year in office.
contrary_evidence: Does not indicate any nuclear-policy choice by Bolsonaro himself.

evidence.claim: Human Rights Watch said political violence, harassment of journalists, and attempts to undermine trust in the electoral system had all increased before the 2022 election, and it pointed to Bolsonaro's false fraud claims and inflammatory rhetoric as part of the risk environment.
evidence.title: Brazil: Uphold the Right to Vote Freely and Safely
evidence.excerpt: Human Rights Watch said political violence, harassment of journalists, and attempts to undermine trust in the electoral system had all increased before the 2022 election, and it pointed to Bolsonaro's false fraud claims and inflammatory rhetoric as part of the risk environment.
evidence.source_locator: Lead paragraphs and the section on Bolsonaro's statements about the election system
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Well-documented rights report with direct quotation and contemporary election context.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly attributable to Bolsonaro's public conduct, while the broader violence environment also involved other actors.
contrary_evidence: The source also notes protective action by electoral authorities, so Bolsonaro was not the only relevant actor in the environment.

evidence.claim: UN experts said threats, intimidation, and political violence were rising online and offline, especially against women, Indigenous Peoples, Afro-descendants, and LGBTI people, and warned that hateful language by candidates and supporters could trigger violence.
evidence.title: Especialistas da ONU clamam por eleições pacíficas no Brasil
evidence.excerpt: UN experts said threats, intimidation, and political violence were rising online and offline, especially against women, Indigenous Peoples, Afro-descendants, and LGBTI people, and warned that hateful language by candidates and supporters could trigger violence.
evidence.source_locator: Body text and quoted statements from the UN experts
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Contemporaneous UN statement with clear attribution and election-specific scope.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Applies to Bolsonaro as an incumbent candidate and chief political actor, though the statement is about the broader campaign environment.
contrary_evidence: It is a warning, not a finding that Bolsonaro ordered specific attacks.

evidence.claim: RSF reported more than 3.3 million offensive and intimidating messages against journalists and the media in the final three months of 2022, about one every three seconds.
evidence.title: A journalist was harassed online every three seconds during Brazil’s election campaign
evidence.excerpt: RSF reported more than 3.3 million offensive and intimidating messages against journalists and the media in the final three months of 2022, about one every three seconds.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Large-scale monitoring study by a specialist press-freedom NGO.
evidence.ruler_attribution: The report frames the violence as rising under Bolsonaro's presidency and during his campaign, but it does not assign every message personally to him.
contrary_evidence: The same data also reflect behavior by supporters and online networks, not just Bolsonaro personally.

evidence.claim: Abraji said attacks against journalists rose 23% in 2022 to 557 episodes, and 41.6% of cases involved at least one Bolsonaro family member.
evidence.title: Ataques mais graves a jornalistas dobraram em 2022
evidence.excerpt: Abraji said attacks against journalists rose 23% in 2022 to 557 episodes, and 41.6% of cases involved at least one Bolsonaro family member.
evidence.source_locator: Report summary in the news release
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Brazilian investigative-journalism association using systematic monitoring data.
evidence.period_fit: Retrospective on 2022, but directly about the target year.
evidence.ruler_attribution: The Bolsonaro-family linkage is explicit, although the report does not claim Bolsonaro personally executed each attack.
contrary_evidence: This is aggregate monitoring, so it does not prove direct personal causation in every case.

evidence.claim: A São Paulo court ordered Bolsonaro to pay collective damages to journalists and said his attacks and threats, as head of state, had helped contribute to virtual and physical attacks on journalists across Brazil.
evidence.title: Bolsonaro é condenado por dano moral coletivo a jornalistas
evidence.excerpt: A São Paulo court ordered Bolsonaro to pay collective damages to journalists and said his attacks and threats, as head of state, had helped contribute to virtual and physical attacks on journalists across Brazil.
evidence.source_locator: Lead paragraph and the judge's quoted reasoning
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Reuters reporting via a major Brazilian outlet, with a precise judicial finding quoted in the article.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly attributable to Bolsonaro's own speech and conduct.
contrary_evidence: The decision was subject to appeal, so it is a legal finding rather than a final criminal judgment.

evidence.claim: During the presidential debate, Bolsonaro told journalist Vera Magalhães she was 'a disgrace to Brazilian journalism' and used sexualized and belittling language that targeted women journalists.
evidence.title: Alvos, Bolsonaro ataca mulheres e Lula fica na defensiva; Tebet é destaque
evidence.excerpt: During the presidential debate, Bolsonaro told journalist Vera Magalhães she was 'a disgrace to Brazilian journalism' and used sexualized and belittling language that targeted women journalists.
evidence.source_locator: Debate transcript excerpt quoted in the story
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Contemporaneous debate reporting with direct quote from Bolsonaro.
contrary_evidence: A single debate episode is not the whole record, but it is materially relevant because it came from the candidate himself.

evidence.claim: Human Rights Watch said Bolsonaro personally amplified efforts to discredit and restrict gender and sexuality education, which contributed to fear and self-censorship among teachers.
evidence.title: Brazil: Attacks on Gender and Sexuality Education
evidence.excerpt: Human Rights Watch said Bolsonaro personally amplified efforts to discredit and restrict gender and sexuality education, which contributed to fear and self-censorship among teachers.
evidence.source_locator: Report summary and quoted HRW finding
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Well-specified rights report grounded in interviews and documentary review.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly attributable to Bolsonaro's political messaging.
contrary_evidence: This is repression by rhetoric and policy climate, not a physical-violence event by itself.

evidence.claim: HRW said the Bolsonaro administration undermined the agency protecting Indigenous rights, weakened environmental enforcement, and emboldened miners, loggers, land-grabbers, and poachers to encroach on Indigenous territories.
evidence.title: Brazil: Indigenous Rights Under Serious Threat
evidence.excerpt: HRW said the Bolsonaro administration undermined the agency protecting Indigenous rights, weakened environmental enforcement, and emboldened miners, loggers, land-grabbers, and poachers to encroach on Indigenous territories.
evidence.source_locator: Opening paragraphs and the section on FUNAI leadership
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Contemporaneous HRW investigation with direct attribution to the administration.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Administration-level policy under Bolsonaro, with direct attribution to his government.
contrary_evidence: The source attributes much of the harm to non-state encroachers, so the ruler link is through policy and tolerance rather than direct violence.

evidence.claim: The Supreme Court suspended parts of Bolsonaro's decrees easing access to guns, saying the election campaign made political violence an urgent risk.
evidence.title: Fachin suspende trechos de decretos de Bolsonaro que ampliam acesso a armas
evidence.excerpt: The Supreme Court suspended parts of Bolsonaro's decrees easing access to guns, saying the election campaign made political violence an urgent risk.
evidence.source_locator: Opening paragraphs summarizing Justice Fachin's injunction
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Accurate contemporaneous reporting of a judicial order and its stated rationale.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly tied to Bolsonaro's decrees and policy agenda.
contrary_evidence: The court, not Bolsonaro, imposed the restraining measure, so this is adverse evidence against him rather than evidence of restraint by him.

evidence.claim: Bolsonaro repeated false claims about the electronic voting system to foreign diplomats and attacked TSE ministers without evidence, months before the election.
evidence.title: Bolsonaro chama embaixadores para atacar processo eleitoral; TSE rebate
evidence.excerpt: Bolsonaro repeated false claims about the electronic voting system to foreign diplomats and attacked TSE ministers without evidence, months before the election.
evidence.source_locator: Lead paragraphs describing the diplomatic event and its contents
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Reuters report with direct description of the president's own remarks.
contrary_evidence: This is incitement and misinformation rather than physical violence, but it materially raised the domestic fear climate.

evidence.claim: After the runoff, Bolsonaro asked supporters to stop blocking highways, while also calling other protests part of democratic life and saying he was with them.
evidence.title: Bolsonaro pede que apoiadores liberem estradas e diz que outros protestos são do 'jogo democrático'
evidence.excerpt: After the runoff, Bolsonaro asked supporters to stop blocking highways, while also calling other protests part of democratic life and saying he was with them.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Reuters report of Bolsonaro's own public message during the roadblock crisis.
evidence.period_fit: Directly after the 2022 election, still within the target year.
contrary_evidence: The message was only partial restraint because it still legitimized the surrounding protest climate.

evidence.claim: Reuters reported allegations that Brazil's Federal Highway Police set up illegal roadblocks to delay voters in Lula-leaning areas, with critics arguing the force had become overtly pro-Bolsonaro.
evidence.title: Brazil highway police blockades fan voter-suppression fears
evidence.excerpt: Reuters reported allegations that Brazil's Federal Highway Police set up illegal roadblocks to delay voters in Lula-leaning areas, with critics arguing the force had become overtly pro-Bolsonaro.
evidence.source_locator: Lead paragraphs and the section on the PRF director's pro-Bolsonaro post
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Reuters reporting on a major election-security incident with contemporaneous details.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Indirect but material ruler link through a federal force operating in Bolsonaro's political orbit.
contrary_evidence: The article reports allegations and fears, not a final legal finding on command responsibility.

evidence.claim: HRW reported that the Bolsonaro administration reduced the federal budget to fight violence against women by 90% in 2022 compared with 2020.
evidence.title: World Report 2023: Brazil
evidence.excerpt: HRW reported that the Bolsonaro administration reduced the federal budget to fight violence against women by 90% in 2022 compared with 2020.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Major rights report drawing on official budget evidence and country monitoring.
evidence.period_fit: Directly about 2022 budget choices under Bolsonaro.
contrary_evidence: Budget cuts do not alone prove all service failure, but they are strong negative evidence for protection capacity.

evidence.claim: The TSE found that Bolsonaro's motociata and temple event in Cuiabá constituted premature campaign propaganda.
evidence.title: TSE multa Jair Bolsonaro, candidato à reeleição à Presidência, por propaganda antecipada
evidence.excerpt: The TSE found that Bolsonaro's motociata and temple event in Cuiabá constituted premature campaign propaganda.
evidence.source_locator: Lead paragraph summarizing the court ruling
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary electoral-court ruling on Bolsonaro's own campaign conduct.
contrary_evidence: A single sanction does not by itself prove a full pattern of capture, but it is directly relevant to manipulation of the campaign environment.

evidence.claim: The TSE barred the use of images from Bolsonaro's official trips in campaign material to preserve equal opportunity in the race.
evidence.title: Imagens de Bolsonaro em viagem como chefe de Estado não podem ser usadas em campanha
evidence.excerpt: The TSE barred the use of images from Bolsonaro's official trips in campaign material to preserve equal opportunity in the race.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary court order directly addressing misuse of official state imagery in the campaign.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly tied to Bolsonaro as incumbent candidate and head of state.
contrary_evidence: The order is a constraint on misuse, not evidence that Bolsonaro voluntarily self-bound.

evidence.claim: The OAS said Brazil's TSE was professional and robust and that the election was conducted in a complex context marked by polarization, disinformation, and attacks on electoral institutions.
evidence.title: OAS Electoral Observation Mission Presents its Preliminary Report following the Second Round of the Elections in Brazil
evidence.excerpt: The OAS said Brazil's TSE was professional and robust and that the election was conducted in a complex context marked by polarization, disinformation, and attacks on electoral institutions.
evidence.source_locator: Press release body and summary of mission findings
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Independent regional election-observation mission with direct contemporaneous reporting.
evidence.period_fit: Directly after the 2022 runoff and before the transition ended.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Mostly institutional baseline, but directly relevant to Bolsonaro because it shows the resilience of the institutions he attacked.
contrary_evidence: The report is preliminary and does not itself quantify Bolsonaro's personal responsibility for the disinformation climate.

evidence.claim: Freedom House said Bolsonaro claimed the voting system was susceptible to fraud, challenged the election results in court in late November, and that the TSE rejected the case as bad faith; it also described the 2022 campaign as marked by disinformation, harassment, and political violence.
evidence.title: Brazil: Freedom in the World 2023 Country Report
evidence.excerpt: Freedom House said Bolsonaro claimed the voting system was susceptible to fraud, challenged the election results in court in late November, and that the TSE rejected the case as bad faith; it also described the 2022 campaign as marked by disinformation, harassment, and political violence.
evidence.source_locator: Key Developments in 2022 and the Electoral Process / D1 sections
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Major comparative democracy report synthesizing target-year events and institutional responses.
evidence.period_fit: Summarizes the target year 2022 with direct relevance to Bolsonaro's campaign conduct.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Direct Bolsonaro conduct on fraud claims; institutional response by the TSE; broader violence environment also involved other actors.
contrary_evidence: The same report says Brazil remained a democracy with competitive elections, so this is erosive conduct rather than outright authoritarian closure.

unresolved_gaps: No direct 2022 Bolsonaro-specific nuclear command, crisis, or near-use choice is evidenced.
Direct forensic proof of hidden self-dealing or office-linked family enrichment remains thin.
Broader durable non-electoral program execution is thinner than the campaign-and-power-retention record.
